title: The Cycle 25 radio excess remains after controls for spot position in matched area models
abstract: We test whether a change in spot position on the solar disc explains the Cycle 25 emission excess at fixed corrected dark area. Common-day monthly fits in January 2011-November 2013 and January 2022-November 2024 use projected and corrected HMI areas to measure the area-weighted mean viewing cosine. At fixed HMI area, the F10.7 rise is 9.94% before the position control and 9.87% after it (conditional 95% interval 4.97 to 15.53). The paired change is -0.056 log percentage points (-1.940 to +0.889). Ground-based radial moments, limb fraction, latitude and group controls also retain an excess. Joint area-position support retains 8.43% but has only nine late months. Mg II rises 1.59% in the main position model; the sunspot-number change is uncertain. The tested disc-position redistribution does not explain the fitted excess under stable measurement scales and the declared response models. Radio-source geometry, facular structure, calibration drift and model error remain open. We provide code, aggregate estimates, a figure, source hashes and external-data retrieval instructions. External observations and dated derived tables remain outside the baseline bundle.
